title: Diversity Optimization for Travelling Salesman Problem via Deep Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Multi-Solution TSP requires diverse yet high-quality solutions.

gap.claim: Existing neural TSP methods mostly target a single optimal solution rather than diverse solutions.

contributions.claim: A deep reinforcement learning neural solver for Multi-Solution TSP with an encoder-decoder structured policy is proposed.
A Relativization Filter is designed to improve encoder robustness to affine transformations of problem instances.
Multi-Attentive Adaptive Active Search is designed to balance solution optimality and diversity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the proposed deep reinforcement learning neural solver as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmark instances report superiority over recent neural baselines across different metrics.
The method is reported to be competitive with state-of-the-art traditional heuristics while being 1.3× to 15× faster.
The method is also reported as applicable to the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural TSP methods generally seek a single optimal solution.
The paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning solver for discovering diverse, high-quality Multi-Solution TSP solutions.
The solver uses a Relativization Filter for affine-transformation robustness and Multi-Attentive Adaptive Active Search for balancing optimality and diversity.
Benchmark experiments report strong performance against neural baselines and competitive traditional heuristics with reduced computational time.
The approach is reported to extend to CVRP.

source_observation.claim: Balancing solution quality and diversity is treated as a decoder-level search objective.

interpretation.claim: Search procedures for multi-solution optimization may need explicit mechanisms that manage competing objectives.

application.claim: For related multi-solution problems, consider adaptive attention or active-search mechanisms that jointly account for quality and diversity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when this balance is preferable to alternative multi-objective optimization strategies.

source_observation.claim: The method is reported to be faster than traditional heuristics by 1.3× to 15× while remaining competitive.

interpretation.claim: Computational efficiency can be a practical complement to solution-quality comparisons in combinatorial optimization.

application.claim: Evaluate optimization methods using both solution metrics and computational time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the hardware, baselines, or evaluation conditions underlying the reported speed range.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, instance sizes, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe training procedures, hyperparameters, or computational hardware.
The abstract does not quantify diversity or optimality outcomes separately.
The abstract does not provide details of the CVRP experiments.
